title: Beef, ribeye, steak, boneless, choice, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Ribeye steak is a cut from the beef rib area, prized for its marbling and rich flavor. This version is boneless, graded "choice" (mid‑range quality) and sold raw, ready for grilling, pan‑searing, or oven cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name "ribeye" comes from the eye‑shaped fatty center that resembles an eye in the rib muscle.
Marbling – the intramuscular fat – makes the steak exceptionally juicy and flavorful when cooked.
Choice grade sits between Prime (highest) and Select (lower) in the U.S. beef grading system.
Traditionally ribeye is cooked "à la française": a quick sear on high heat followed by finishing to the desired doneness.
In the United States ribeye is often served simply with salt, black pepper, and a pat of butter.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids, making it an excellent source of complete protein for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat supplies highly bioavailable heme iron and zinc, important for immune function and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ribeye contains B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which support nervous system health and metabolic processes.

items.title: Creatine source
items.content: Creatine in beef helps increase muscular energy during high‑intensity exercise.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: The marbled fat includes monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that, in moderation, can support heart health.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive consumption of red meat may raise cholesterol levels; moderation is recommended.

items.title: Food‑borne pathogen risk
items.content: Raw beef can harbor E. coli, Salmonella and other pathogens; cook to a safe internal temperature.

items.title: Beef allergy or sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef proteins.

items.title: Histamine formation
items.content: If stored too long, meat can accumulate histamine, which may cause food‑related reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: For a medium‑rare ribeye, sear on high heat 2‑3 minutes per side, then let rest 5‑10 minutes. Season simply with salt, black pepper, and finish with butter and rosemary in the pan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw beef refrigerated at 0‑2 °C in an airtight package for 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
